title: Tech Note: 4D Live Window JavaScript Part 1 – Offscreen Areas
author: Josh Fletcher, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note describes a workaround for a technical limitation of the 4D Live Window plug-in: since 4DLW could not create a true offscreen browser area, the author instead hides a Palette window containing a 4DLW area off the visible screen, letting JavaScript functions loaded in it be called like a code library via Web_JavaScriptReturn and a custom interprocess event model. It is a clever but very plug-in- and Windows-specific hack (JavaScript execution in 4DLW never worked reliably on Mac OS) built entirely on the discontinued 4D Web 2.0 Pack; the concrete commands and window-hiding technique have no modern equivalent since 4D Live Window no longer exists. The general idea of treating a JavaScript engine as a reusable calculation library from 4D code is still conceptually interesting but would today be solved very differently.
related_updates: 4D Live Window and 4D Web 2.0 Pack were discontinued and are no longer part of any current 4D product
Any need to call JavaScript logic from 4D code today would use 4D's built-in JSON/JavaScript-adjacent commands or an external Node.js/HTTP service rather than a hidden browser plug-in window
